# Tools

## TxSuite

TxSuite is T5Suite, T7Suite and T8Suite in one program, for Windows, Linux and macOS.
For a T7 it has the following functions:

- Checksum verification and correction (Actions → Verify checksum, and every time it writes a map)
- Software ID adjustment (Actions → Firmware information)
- Immobilizer code and chassis ID (VIN) adjustment (Actions → Firmware information)
- Firmware options like Open SID info and the torque limiters (Actions → Firmware information)
- What the SID shows (Actions → SID information)
- ESP calibration and the TCM limit (Actions → ESP calibration and TCM limit)
- Extraction of symbol table (when it opens a file)
- Map visualization and editing (the map viewer)
- Compare maps in binary to another binary (Actions → Compare symbols with other binary)
- Move maps from one binary to another (Actions → Transfer maps to another binary)
- Tuning packages (File → Import tuning package and Edit a tuning package)
- Airmass result viewer (Actions → Airmass result viewer)
- Downloading flash content from ECU through Canbus (ECU → Read ECU)
- Flashing ECU through Canbus (ECU → Flash current file to ECU)
- SRAM snapshots and comparing them (ECU → Get SRAM snapshot and the Actions menu)
- Realtime viewing and logging, and real-time tuning on open software (Realtime menu)
- AFR feedback maps from a wideband (Realtime → AFR maps and Actions → Import AFR feedback data)
- Projects that log every change, with roll back and roll forward (File → Project)

It can be downloaded from <https://github.com/roffe/TuningSuites/releases/latest>.
For usage of this tool please refer to its user manual, Help → T7 → User manual.

## BD32

BD32.exe is the tool used to interface with the ECU through a BDM interface.
It is DOS based and will run normally on Win95/98/Me.
Ideally the user would boot into a DOS environment to use the tool.
There is a windows version available but the author has no experience with that specific tool.

## IDA Pro {.advanced}

IDAPro stands for Interactive DisAssembler Professional.
It enables the user to disassemble binary files to its original source code.
IDAPro is commercial software, not freeware.

Example of how to use IDA Pro with a **Trionic 7** box.\
Open binary/raw file\
Set processor to Motorola series: 68330\
Check the 'Create RAM section', start address 0xF00000, size 0xFFFF.\
Go to address ROM:00000000 in 'IDA View-A' and hit D-key three times to get dc.l \$FFFFEFFC\
Go to the next address ROM:00000004 and hit D-key three times to get reset vector address (this varies from binary to binary)\
You should get e.g. dc.l unk_5169A or something like that, double-click the unk_5169A text\
Your now in the place where the code execution starts, press C to disassemble\
Now, from the menu select Options -> General, go to Analysis tab and press 'Kernel options1' button\
Check 'Make final analysis pass' and hit OK\
Press 'Reanalyze program' button and wait a while (this really takes some time, a minute or so)

TxSuite's File → Generate Idc file writes an IDC script with the symbol names of the open file, to name the addresses in IDA Pro.

## Hex editor {.advanced}

Hexworkshop (or UltraEdit) is a tool that comes in handy often.
It can be used to view, search and modify the raw binary file.
TxSuite has one built in, Actions → View file in hex.
